tests spawn `node --import=tsx/esm` against a real docgen.config.ts, and tsx is
a devDependency of apps/validate that pnpm does not hoist to the root, so those
jobs were failing on `Cannot find package 'tsx'` with a Rust-only toolchain.

zizmor itself runs as a CI job and as `just zizmor`, unconditionally: a
workflow edit is exactly what no language-scoped job would catch.

dependabot.yml covers github-actions, cargo, and npm weekly, with a 7-day
cooldown so a yanked crate or pulled action release surfaces before it lands
here. Routine and security updates are separate groups per ecosystem, and the
oxc_* crates get their own group -- they release in lockstep and break APIs in
minor versions, so they have to move together or not at all.

---
oxc-react-docgen-core: patch
---

String-literal union aliases now report bare member values. A `type Size = "sm" | "md"` alias previously came back with each member already quoted, so serialized output showed `""sm"" | ""md""` and a template literal over the alias expanded to `compact-"sm"`. `undefined` members are dropped (optionality is reported through `required`); a `null` member keeps the alias a plain union, since a string-only literal union can't represent it.

cat > /tmp/pr-body.md <<'MD'
Started as the proto-only toolchain fix; grew to cover everything that was stale or broken around it, plus three extraction fixes that were already in flight.

CI on this branch was red before these commits, for two unrelated reasons, both fixed here:

- All six TypeScript/Install/Format jobs failed with `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE` — `ef8cec9` changed `packages/cli/package.json` without regenerating `pnpm-lock.yaml`.
- Test and Coverage failed with `Cannot find package 'tsx'` — `crates/cli`'s config tests spawn `node --import=tsx/esm` against a real `docgen.config.ts`, and `tsx` is a devDependency of `apps/validate` that pnpm doesn't hoist, so a Rust-only job has no `node_modules`.

## Extraction fixes

**Ambient `.d.ts` files are merged for their types, not their components.** `@types/react` declares `class PureComponent<P, S, SS> extends Component<P, S, SS>`, which matched the class-component detector, so full HTML-attribute mode emitted `PureComponent` as a ghost 0-prop component plus a `Cannot resolve type 'P'` diagnostic. Covered in both the batch pipeline and `WatchSession::initialize`, which builds its first revision through the same merge.

**Literal-union alias members are stored bare.** `ts_type_to_collected` built members with `to_raw_string()`, which quotes; every serializer quotes again, so `type Size = "sm" | "md"` rendered as `""sm"" | ""md""` and a template literal over it expanded to `compact-"sm"`. `undefined` is dropped (optionality lives in `required`), `null` keeps the alias a plain `Union`. `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` goes to 4 — the cache key is a content hash and can't notice the extractor now produces different data for identical input.

**`--format rdt` omits an undocumented `children`**, matching RDT's default `skipChildrenPropWithoutDoc`. `--format canonical` keeps it.

Three changesets, all patch.

## callisto 0.8

0.8 removed the action's `publish` input: `callisto-action` only creates the release PR now, and publication runs from the merged release commit under this repo's own workflow. The old one-step job would have silently published nothing. `release.yml` becomes that workflow — verified-merge detection → `callisto release plan --from-release-commit` → `callisto release execute` behind a `release` environment that is the only place registry credentials exist, with the intent passed between jobs as a same-run artifact plus SHA-256 sidecar.

Two latent bugs found on the way: `callisto.toml` used `publish-to = "cratesIo"` where the parser accepts `crates-io`, so the entire config failed to load and no per-package override was ever applied; and the private root `package.json` was named `oxc-react-docgen`, colliding with the CLI crate and making every `oxc-react-docgen: patch` changeset ambiguous across cargo and npm.

## Toolchain

`.moon/toolchain.yml` is the moon 1.x filename — v2 renamed it to `toolchains.yml`, so moon has been ignoring the whole file, including a `pnpm: "10"` that contradicted `.prototools`. Rewritten in v2 shape with versions inherited from `.prototools`. moon 2.3.3 → 2.4.5 (not 2.5.5: that needs proto ≥ 0.60.0). Rust 1.96.0 → 1.98.1, whose clippy caught two real `question_mark` sites.

**After pulling, run `moon sync vcs-hooks`** — the pre-commit hook's command list moved into a `just pre-commit` recipe.

## CI and supply chain

zizmor reported 30 findings: `ci.yml` declared no `permissions:` at all, and ten checkouts left credentials in `.git/config`. Now `permissions: {}` at workflow scope with `contents: read` per job, `persist-credentials: false` everywhere, and one inline ignore for the deliberate lockfile-free install test. Every action is SHA-pinned and bumped (checkout v7.0.1, upload-artifact v7.0.1, download-artifact v8.0.1, codecov v7.1.1, cargo-deny v2.1.1, setup-toolchain v0.6.4). zizmor runs as a CI job and as `just zizmor`.

Dependabot covers github-actions, cargo, and npm weekly with a 7-day cooldown, routine and security updates in separate groups, and `oxc_*` in a group of its own since those crates break APIs in minor releases and must move together.

## Dependencies

Snapshot `fileName`s embed the pnpm store path with its exact version, so one `@types/react` bump rewrote all seven fixtures — with weekly dependabot PRs that churn would bury real changes, so `snapshots.rs` now redacts it to `[VERSION]`, unit-tested against scoped, peer-suffixed, repeated, absent, and versionless segments.

Eight dead `[workspace.dependencies]` entries removed (declared, referenced by no crate). criterion 0.8, rstest 0.27, trycmd 1.2. `compact_str` deliberately stays at 0.9 to share `oxc_span`'s copy. `deny.toml`'s eight `skip` entries are all reported unnecessary now that `oxc_module_lexer` is gone. npm: `@types/node` ^22 → ^26, vite ^8 + vitest ^5 — the plugin advertised `vite: ^7 || ^8` but only tested against 7.

## Not here

**oxc 0.135 → 0.151** is a separate PR. Attempted and reverted: 15 compile errors in the core extractor — `Class.super_class`/`super_type_arguments`, `ExportNamedDeclaration.declaration`/`.source`, `TSModuleDeclaration` and `TSModuleDeclarationName` (gone from the AST and the `Visit` trait), `ParserReturn.errors`, `TSInterfaceHeritage.expression`. It touches ambient-module, export, and class-heritage handling and needs snapshot review on its own. `oxc_span` 0.151 also moves to `compact_str` 0.10, which is why that bump isn't in this PR.

Also left alone: TypeScript 5.9 → 7.0, react-docgen 7 → 8 (it's the accuracy-comparison baseline), chalk 5 → 6, pnpm 11 → 12.

## Verification

`cargo fmt/clippy -D warnings/nextest (537)/doc -D warnings/deny/machete`, `typos`, `zizmor`, `callisto validate`, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, vite-plugin build + 33 tests.

git add -A -- Cargo.toml Cargo.lock crates/core/src && git commit -q -F - > /dev/null 2>&1 <<'MSG'
feat(deps): migrate to oxc 0.151

oxc restructured three AST areas between 0.135 and 0.151. All seven fixture
snapshots are byte-identical after the port, so extraction behavior is
unchanged.

Export declarations split three ways. The old `ExportNamedDeclaration` carried
an optional `declaration`, optional `source`, and a specifier list, and one
visitor matched its way between them. It is now `ExportDeclaration`
(`export const X`), `ExportNamedDeclaration` (`export { X }`), and
`ExportFromDeclaration` (`export { X } from "y"`), so the match disappears into
three visitors. `is_type_only` on an inline declaration export stays false:
`export_kind` only ever marked the `type` in `export type { A }`, which is a
specifier list, and deriving it from the declaration's own kind would be wrong
for `export enum`, which declares a runtime value.

`TSModuleDeclaration` split by how the module is named --
`TSNamespaceDeclaration` (`namespace Foo`), `TSExternalModuleDeclaration`
(`declare module "pkg"`), `TSGlobalDeclaration` (`declare global`). Only the
first qualifies the names declared inside it, which the old string-literal arm
expressed by declining to push onto the namespace stack; the other two now need
no override at all.

`Class.super_class` and `super_type_arguments` merged into one
`Class.heritage`, and `TSInterfaceHeritage.expression: Expression` became
`type_name: TSTypeName` -- so heritage names now go through the shared
`ts_type_name_str` walk instead of a second pattern match over member
expressions. `ParserReturn::errors` is now `diagnostics`.

compact_str moves to 0.10 with oxc_span, which also drops it out of the
duplicate-version list: oxc_resolver 11.24 already wanted 0.10 while oxc_span
0.135 pinned 0.9.

Two tests cover the splits, both asserting the exact resulting set rather than
that each variant appears somewhere -- a specifier list quietly classified as a
re-export would satisfy a presence check.

input.command:
cat > /tmp/oxc-pr.md <<'MD'
Stacked on #3 — review that first; this branch is `feat/oxc-0.151` against `fix/proto-only-toolchain-setup`.

oxc 0.135 → 0.151. **All seven fixture snapshots are byte-identical after the port**, so extraction behavior is unchanged — this is a pure API migration.

## What moved

**Export declarations split three ways.** The old `ExportNamedDeclaration` carried an optional `declaration`, an optional `source`, and a specifier list, and one visitor matched its way between them. It's now three nodes:

| node | syntax |
|---|---|
| `ExportDeclaration` | `export const X` / `export interface X` |
| `ExportNamedDeclaration` | `export { X }` |
| `ExportFromDeclaration` | `export { X } from "y"` |

The match disappears into three visitors. One judgment call worth checking: `is_type_only` on an inline declaration export stays `false`. `export_kind` never described the declaration — it marks the `type` in `export type { A }`, which is a specifier list and arrives as `ExportNamedDeclaration`. Deriving it from the declaration's own kind would be a behavior change, and would be wrong for `export enum`, which declares a runtime value.

**`TSModuleDeclaration` split by how the module is named** — `TSNamespaceDeclaration` (`namespace Foo`), `TSExternalModuleDeclaration` (`declare module "pkg"`), `TSGlobalDeclaration` (`declare global`). Only the first qualifies the names declared inside it. The old code expressed that by declining to push the string-literal case onto the namespace stack; the other two now need no visitor override at all.

**`Class.super_class` + `super_type_arguments` → one `Class.heritage`**, and **`TSInterfaceHeritage.expression: Expression` → `type_name: TSTypeName`**. The second is a real improvement: heritage names now go through the shared `ts_type_name_str` walk instead of a second pattern match over member expressions, so a qualified name like `A.B<T>` is structurally guaranteed rather than reconstructed.

**`ParserReturn::errors` → `diagnostics`.**

## Tests

Two new tests, both asserting the exact resulting set rather than that each variant appears somewhere — the existing `test_exports_collected` is a presence check, and a specifier list quietly classified as a re-export would still satisfy it:

- `every_export_form_lands_in_the_right_lexed_export_variant` — pins locals, named re-exports, and star re-exports across all three new nodes, including `export type { ButtonProps } from` staying type-only.
- `only_an_identifier_named_namespace_qualifies_the_types_declared_inside_it` — pins that `namespace Theme` qualifies its members while `declare module "pkg"` and `declare global` do not.

## Side effect

`compact_str` goes to 0.10 with `oxc_span` and drops out of cargo-deny's duplicate list — `oxc_resolver` 11.24 already wanted 0.10 while `oxc_span` 0.135 pinned 0.9. That's why #3 deliberately left `compact_str` at 0.9.

## Verification

`cargo fmt/clippy -D warnings/nextest (539)/doc -D warnings/deny/machete`, `typos`.

input.command:
git status --short | grep -v "^??" && git add .prototools pnpm-workspace.yaml pnpm-lock.yaml && git commit -q -F - > /dev/null 2>&1 <<'MSG'
fix(ci): make a clean pnpm install reproducible

`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` has never been able to pass on a clean tree,
which is the only kind CI ever has. Two causes, both invisible locally because
an install over an existing node_modules is a no-op that never re-compares
anything.

packages/cli and packages/napi declare optionalDependencies on their own
per-platform artifact packages -- @oxc-react-docgen/cli-darwin-arm64 and the
rest. Those are published by the release pipeline, which has never run, so none
of them exist on the registry. pnpm cannot record an unresolvable specifier in
the lockfile, but `--frozen-lockfile` still compares the manifest's specifiers
against it and fails with "5 dependencies were added". Regenerating the
lockfile does not help; it produces the same empty importer. They are now in
`ignoredOptionalDependencies`, which governs only this workspace's own install
-- the published manifests keep their optionalDependencies, which is how a
consumer gets the right binary.

pnpm is pinned exactly rather than to `~11`. CI resolved that to 11.27.1 while
this machine had 11.9.0, so the two were never running the same resolver
against the same lockfile. That is the same drift this branch set out to remove
for node; leaving pnpm floating kept a version mismatch in the one place a
lockfile makes it fatal.

Verified the way CI sees it: `git archive HEAD` into an empty directory, then
`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`.

**Only `check` exposes `--strict` as a CLI flag; `extract`, `watch`, and `inspect` always call `exit_code(false)`.** This asymmetry is intentional but only loosely documented. `docs/root-cause-analysis.md` cluster 11 explicitly preserves it ("note `check.rs` additionally supports a `--strict` warnings-escalate-to-1 path that `extract.rs`'s args have no equivalent flag for today; preserve that distinction rather than assuming the two commands' checks are fully identical"), and `docs/edge-cases.md` P3-1 separately flags the consequence: "`watch` always exits 0 regardless of extraction errors — fine for an interactive dev loop, but a footgun if ever run non-interactively (CI, pre-commit)." So the asymmetry is a deliberate, load-bearing design choice for `check` (whose whole purpose per its doc comment is "For CI"), but it is **not** independently justified anywhere for why `extract`/`watch`/`inspect` shouldn't also grow a `--strict` flag — P3-1 marks it as an accepted-but-unresolved gap rather than a closed decision. Treat "should `extract --strict` exist" as an open question, not a settled one, if it comes up again.

Every one of the five entry points wraps its real body in `oxc_react_docgen_core::panic_guard::contain_panic(label, closure)`. This is not incidental defense — it is a deliberate, documented design decision (`docs/adr/0005-panic-containment-boundary.md`) with a specific and non-obvious shape:

- **The three `spawn_blocking`-wrapped entry points** (`extract_all`, `initialize_session`, `extract_file_incremental`) put `contain_panic` **inside** the `spawn_blocking` closure, not around it. Before ADR 0005, these three were only accidentally panic-safe: `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`'s `JoinError` happens to catch an unwind as a side effect of tokio's own plumbing, not because anyone decided panic-safety belonged there. Wrapping in `contain_panic` too makes the guarantee a designed one, converts the panic into a `Diagnostic`-derived `napi::Error` message instead of an opaque `JoinError`, and stops being contingent on tokio's internals never changing.

-- **`create_session` and `close_session` get `contain_panic` directly**, with no `spawn_blocking` at all, because they run synchronously on the thread the JS call arrived on. Before ADR 0005 these two had **zero** panic protection — not even the accidental kind — documented as an open, unconfirmed risk in `docs/edge-cases.md` P1-9 ("*(Needs verification, not confirmed)*... Whether a panic here crashes the Node process depends on whether napi-rs's codegen auto-wraps in `catch_unwind`"). ADR 0005 closes that gap directly rather than relying on napi-rs's opt-in `#[napi(catch_unwind)]` attribute (considered and rejected in the ADR's "Alternatives considered" section, in favor of one mechanism — `contain_panic` — shared across rayon, plugin hooks, and FFI instead of two different ones). **Note for future readers of `docs/edge-cases.md`: P1-9 as currently written is stale** — it describes a state ADR 0005 has since fixed; it should be marked resolved rather than open next time that document is touched.

## Why this crate's panic discipline is higher-stakes than `crates/cli`'s

-`panic_guard::contain_panic` is shared code — the same function backs rayon `.map()` closures in `pipeline/mod.rs`, `DocgenPlugin` hook calls in `plugin.rs`, and all five entry points here. But the failure mode on the other side of an *uncaught* panic differs by boundary. `crates/cli` is a standalone binary process: an uncaught panic there kills one CLI invocation, and the OS process boundary means nothing else is affected. This crate is a `cdylib` loaded **in-process** into a long-running Node.js server (a Vite dev server, per the doc comments on `create_session`/`initialize_session`/`close_session` referencing `configResolved`/`configureServer`/`buildEnd`). An uncaught Rust panic crossing the FFI boundary here does not fail one call — it is undefined behavior at best and a hard crash of the entire Node process at worst, taking down every other request the dev server was serving. That asymmetry is why `contain_panic` at this boundary is load-bearing in a way it is only "good hygiene" for `crates/cli`: bypass it here and the blast radius is the whole host process, not one invocation.

-- `PropType` — resolved output type at the *type level* (an interface reference becomes a bare `PropType::Named`, never expanded here).

-- `ResolvedChain` (`resolver/mod.rs`) — resolved output at the *chain/component level*: `props: Vec<ParsedProp>`, `inheritance: Vec<InheritedLayer>`, `composes: Vec<String>`, `discriminant_prop: Option<String>`. This is the accumulator a props-providing type (interface, intersection, discriminated union) produces; it's private to the resolver module (`struct ResolvedChain`, not `pub`).

-**Invariant 1 — an interface name resolves differently depending on which level asked.** At the type level (`resolve_named`, called for a *field's* type — e.g. `value: SomeInterface`), a matched interface returns `PropType::Named { name, args }` — bare, unexpanded. At the chain level (`resolve_props_chain`, called for a *props-base* type — the component's own props type, or an `extends` target), the same interface expands via `resolve_interface_chain` into real `ParsedProp`s. This split exists because a field whose type happens to be an interface should show as a named type reference in RDT-compatible output, not get flattened into an anonymous object — but a component's *own* props type (or something it extends) must actually contribute fields. Conflating the two would either over-expand nested interface-typed fields into inline objects, or under-expand a component's own extends chain.

4. `resolve_known` — the hardcoded library-pattern shortcut table in `known.rs` (SxProps, VariantProps, HTMLChakraProps, …).

-**Why this order, and why it's locked:** a project can legitimately declare its own `interface SxProps { customSx: string }` that has nothing to do with MUI. If `known.rs`'s hardcoded SxProps shortcut were checked before the project's own source, that project-defined interface would be silently replaced by the opaque MUI shortcut — the component's real, resolvable prop (`customSx`) would vanish with no trace. `named.rs` always had this order right and documented it as intentional. `chain.rs`'s `extends`-clause path (used when a project's `interface Foo extends SomeName`) independently re-implemented the same sequence and got it backwards — checking `resolve_known` *before* the project's own interface/alias lookup. input.command:
python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p=Path(".github/workflows/ci.yml"); s=p.read_text()
start=s.index("      - run: pnpm --filter @oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin pack --out-dir /tmp/packed\n")
end=s.index("            console.log('OK');\n          \"\n", start)+len("            console.log('OK');\n          \"\n")
new='''      # pnpm 11 removed `pack --out-dir`; `--pack-destination` replaces it.
      - run: pnpm --filter @oxc-react-docgen/napi --filter @oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin pack --pack-destination /tmp/packed

      - name: Install via ${{ matrix.pm }}
        # zizmor: ignore[adhoc-packages] installing the freshly packed tarball
        # outside a lockfile is the point of this job -- it proves a real
        # consumer gets @oxc-react-docgen/napi as a transitive dependency.
        env:
          PM: ${{ matrix.pm }}
        # @oxc-react-docgen/napi isn't on the registry until the first release,
        # so a plain install 404s. An override serves it from its own tarball;
        # it still arrives only because vite-plugin depends on it. pnpm 11 reads
        # overrides from pnpm-workspace.yaml, not package.json.
        run: |
          mkdir /tmp/install-test && cd /tmp/install-test
          napi=$(ls /tmp/packed/oxc-react-docgen-napi-*.tgz)
          plugin=$(ls /tmp/packed/oxc-react-docgen-vite-plugin-*.tgz)
          if [ "$PM" = "npm" ]; then
            printf '{"private":true,"overrides":{"@oxc-react-docgen/napi":"file:%s"}}\\n' "$napi" > package.json
            npm install "$plugin"
          else
            echo '{"private":true}' > package.json
            printf 'overrides:\\n  "@oxc-react-docgen/napi": "file:%s"\\n' "$napi" > pnpm-workspace.yaml
            pnpm add "$plugin"
          fi

      # Resolve napi the way vite-plugin's own `require` would, not by a fixed
      # top-level path: pnpm doesn't hoist transitive deps into node_modules/.
      - name: Verify napi is a transitive dependency
        working-directory: /tmp/install-test
        run: |
          node -e "
            const pkg = require('./package.json');
            if (pkg.dependencies && pkg.dependencies['@oxc-react-docgen/napi'])
              throw new Error('napi is a direct dependency; the check proves nothing');
            const plugin = require.resolve('@oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin/package.json');
            require.resolve('@oxc-react-docgen/napi/package.json', { paths: [plugin] });
            console.log('OK');
          "
'''
s=s[:start]+new+s[end:]
p.write_text(s)
PY

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

content.thinking: Found the cause: the step moves to /tmp/install-test outside the repo, so proto's pnpm shim can't find the `.prototools` pin (npm works fine since PROTO_NODE_VERSION comes from the matrix). I'll fix it by capturing the pinned pnpm version before leaving the repo.

input.command:
python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p=Path(".github/workflows/ci.yml"); s=p.read_text()
old="""        run: |
          mkdir /tmp/install-test && cd /tmp/install-test
          napi=$(ls /tmp/packed/oxc-react-docgen-napi-*.tgz)"""
new="""        run: |
          # proto resolves pnpm from .prototools, which /tmp/install-test is
          # outside of; carry the repo's pinned version across the cd.
          PROTO_PNPM_VERSION="$(pnpm --version)"
          export PROTO_PNPM_VERSION
          mkdir /tmp/install-test && cd /tmp/install-test
          napi=$(ls /tmp/packed/oxc-react-docgen-napi-*.tgz)"""
assert old in s
p.write_text(s.replace(old,new,1))
PY

the repo, so proto's pnpm shim finds no .prototools and fails to detect a
version. npm was unaffected: the matrix sets PROTO_NODE_VERSION. Export

cargo clippy --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings 2>&1 | tail -1 && cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --locked 2>&1 | grep -E "FAIL|Summary" && cat > .changeset/dts-cache-concurrent-writes.md <<'MD'
---
oxc-react-docgen-core: patch
---

Concurrent runs sharing one DTS cache directory — the CLI and the Vite plugin in the same project, or parallel builds — no longer report a spurious `IO_ERROR` "Failed to persist the DTS cache" diagnostic. Every writer used the same temp file name, so the second rename found it already moved. Temp names are now unique per process and write.
MD
git add crates/core/src/cache.rs .changeset/dts-cache-concurrent-writes.md && git commit -q -F - >/dev/null 2>&1 <<'MSG'
fix(core): give each DTS cache write its own temp file

try_save wrote through a fixed `dts-v1.msgpack.tmp`. Processes sharing a cache
dir -- the CLI and Vite plugin in one project, parallel builds, nextest's
per-test processes -- overwrote each other's temp file, and whichever renamed
second failed with ENOENT, surfacing an IO_ERROR diagnostic on a run whose
extraction was fine. It showed up as a flaky snapshot_mantine in CI, where the
diagnostic landed in the snapshot.

The temp name now carries the pid and a per-process sequence number, a failed
rename removes its temp file, and manifest.json goes through the same atomic
path instead of a bare fs::write that concurrent writers could interleave.

The new test runs 16 concurrent writers on one dir: it fails 5/5 against the
fixed name and passes 5/5 with the fix.

entries.name: PushNotification
entries.description:
This tool sends a desktop notification in the user's terminal. If Remote Control is connected, it also pushes to their phone. Either way, it pulls their attention from whatever they're doing — a meeting, another task, dinner — to this session. That's the cost. The benefit is they learn something now that they'd want to know now: a long task finished while they were away, a build is ready, you've hit something that needs their decision before you can continue.

Because a notification they didn't need is annoying in a way that accumulates, err toward not sending one. Don't notify for routine progress, or to announce you've answered something they asked seconds ago and are clearly still watching, or when a quick task completes. Notify when there's a real chance they've walked away and there's something worth coming back for — or when they've explicitly asked you to notify them.

Keep the message under 200 characters, one line, no markdown. Lead with what they'd act on — "build failed: 2 auth tests" tells them more than "task done" and more than a status dump.

When the user is actively at the terminal, your output already reaches them — a notification on top of it would be a duplicate, so the tool skips it and says so. A "not sent" result is expected and only ever about this one notification: it was redundant, turned off, or had nowhere to go.

Never wrap commit message lines at 80 characters or any other limit. Let lines be as long as they need to be.

Commit messages must be: meaningful, friendly, scannable, engineering-focused, and succinct.

**Why:** The user explicitly called out AI word salad and AI slop as things to avoid. Long wrapped paragraphs, filler phrases, and verbose "explanation of what the code does" prose are all symptoms of this.

**How to apply:**
- Subject line: imperative, specific, ≤72 chars preferred but never truncate meaning
- Body (if needed): one or two sentences max — the WHY, not the WHAT

full = lambda s: git("rev-parse", s).strip()
msgs = {
 "1d7301a": "fix(core): merge ambient .d.ts files for their types, not their components\n\nIn full HTML-attribute mode, @types/react's `PureComponent<P, ...>` was detected as a 0-prop component with an unresolvable `P`.",
 "e7b6289": "fix(core): store literal-union alias members bare instead of pre-quoted\n\nSerializers quote members themselves, so `\"sm\" | \"md\"` rendered as `\"\"sm\"\"`. Cache schema bumped to 4: the content-hash key can't detect extractor output changes.",
 "d3e544a": "feat(cli): omit undocumented children from --format rdt\n\nMatches RDT's default `skipChildrenPropWithoutDoc`; `--format canonical` keeps it.",
 "e22b137": "docs: retarget type-checker plans at shipped TypeScript 7, correct LSP status\n\nSTATUS.md claimed LSP hovers; the command is a scaffold with `hoverProvider: false`.",
 "d760bce": "fix(release): adopt callisto 0.8's release-PR and durable-execute split\n\n0.8 dropped the action's `publish` input, so the old job published nothing. Also fixes callisto.toml's invalid `cratesIo` value (the config never loaded) and the root package name colliding with the CLI crate.",
 "c2740d9": "chore(toolchain): migrate moon config to v2, raise Rust to 1.98.1\n\nmoon 2 renamed toolchain.yml to toolchains.yml, so the old file was silently ignored. moon stays at 2.4.5: 2.5 needs proto >= 0.60.",
 "b4d3034": "ci: pin actions by SHA, harden permissions, add zizmor and dependabot\n\nzizmor flagged jobs with default token scope and checkouts persisting credentials. Rust test jobs now install the workspace because config tests spawn tsx.",
 "a5d2656": "chore(deps): refresh cargo and npm dependencies\n\nSnapshots now redact pnpm store versions so dependency bumps don't rewrite them. Drops 8 unused workspace deps; compact_str stays at 0.9 to match oxc_span.",
 "7c011ef": "chore(changeset): add changesets for the extraction fixes",
 "c288701": "fix(ci): make a clean frozen pnpm install pass\n\nUnpublished platform optionalDependencies can't be locked, so frozen installs failed on every clean tree. pnpm pinned exactly: CI resolved `~11` to a different version than local.",
 "cb91bb3": "style: format markdown, disable oxlint one-var\n\nMarkdown was already unformatted on main, hidden by the lockfile failure. oxlint 1.83 added `one-var` to the style category.",
 "159884e": "fix(ci): make the transitive-install job runnable before the first release\n\npnpm 11 removed `pack --out-dir`. napi is unpublished, so it's served via override and still arrives only transitively.",
 "4f9d0e7": "fix(core): give each DTS cache write its own temp file\n\nWith a fixed temp name, processes sharing a cache dir clobbered each other's temp file and the second rename failed with a spurious IO_ERROR.",
}
squash = {"159884e": ["122f648"], "4f9d0e7": ["a66025e", "c3abaff"], "a5d2656": ["c1d16ef"], "c2740d9": ["fbc7203"]}
order = git("rev-list","--reverse","--abbrev-commit","--abbrev=7","0b6816a..HEAD").split()
skip = {x for v in squash.values() for x in v}
todo=[]
for c in order:
    if c in skip: continue
    todo.append(f"pick {c}")
    group=[c]+squash.get(c,[])
    for f in squash.get(c,[]): todo.append(f"fixup {f}")
    trailers=[]
    for g in group:
        for line in git("log","-1","--format=%B",g).splitlines():
            if line.startswith("Entire-Checkpoint:") and line not in trailers: trailers.append(line)
    body = msgs[c] + ("\n\n" + "\n".join(trailers) if trailers else "") + "\n"
    open(f"/tmp/rw/{c}","w").write(body)
    todo.append(f"exec git commit --amend --no-verify -q -F /tmp/rw/{c}")
open("/tmp/rw/todo","w").write("\n".join(todo)+"\n")
print("\n".join(todo))
PY

git push -q -u origin fix/ts7-lib-resolution 2>&1 | grep -v entire; cat > /tmp/pr-ts7.md <<'MD'
#8 moved `main` to TypeScript 7.0.2, which broke `test_indexed_access_into_ambient_dom_interface_resolves_via_real_lib` in Test and Coverage on every PR (#9, #10).

It's a real product bug, not a test issue: TS 7 ships `lib.dom.d.ts`/`lib.es5.d.ts` in the installed `@typescript/typescript-<platform>` optional dependency, and both packages' `exports` hide `./lib`. `typescript/lib/lib.dom.d.ts` no longer resolves, so DOM/ES globals (`HTMLDivElement["dir"]`, `Date`, …) silently stopped resolving for any user on TS 7.

#6 is closed. #7's conflicts are resolved, but Dependabot has since replaced #7 with #10. #10 still can't merge green: Test and Coverage now fail on every PR because `main` broke.

- **#6: closed.** It moved oxc to 0.150, but `main` is already on 0.151 from #4, so merging it would have been a downgrade.
- **#7 → #10:** I rebuilt #7 on `main` and pushed it, then Dependabot closed it and opened #10 with the same two bumps (comfy-table 7→8, crossterm 0.28→0.29). #10 has no conflicts and needs no code changes.
- **Why Test/Coverage fail:** #8, a Dependabot npm update merged meanwhile, moved `main` to TypeScript 7.0.2. TypeScript 7 moved its `lib.dom.d.ts` / `lib.es5.d.ts` files into a separate per-platform package that blocks access to them. So in any project on TypeScript 7, DOM and built-in types like `HTMLDivElement` and `Date` quietly stopped resolving. That's a real bug for users, not just a broken test.
- **#11 fixes it** (branched from `main`): when TypeScript's old file location doesn't resolve, the resolver finds the installed platform package and reads the files from there. New tests cover the old layout, the TypeScript 7 layout, and no TypeScript at all; switching the fix off makes them fail. All 543 tests pass locally with TypeScript 7 installed. Changeset added. CI is running and I'm watching it.

Once #11 merges, #9 and #10 need their checks re-run (or a rebase) to go green.

- snapshot: Update and review snapshot tests.
- courier:changeset: Trigger when the user asks to add a changeset or document a change: "add a changeset", "document this change", "what changed here". Extracts the consumer-facing meaning of a diff: classifies consumer_impact (behavior-change, new-capability, internal-only) and semver_impact (major, minor, patch, none) per shared/references/delivery/changesets.md's decision table, then writes a summary scaled to that classification. A diff spanning multiple independent topics — common on a backlog/catch-up run, not just a single PR — produces one changeset per topic, not one bundled entry. When the change came via smith, pass along implementer's criteria_evidence — changeset-analyzer uses those exact locations instead of reconstructing approximate ones from the diff.
- courier:commit: Trigger when the user asks to commit code or write a commit message: "commit this", "write a commit message", "commit the staged changes". Reads the staged git diff and produces a conventional commit message explaining why the change was made, not what changed — the diff already shows what changed.
- courier:post-review: Trigger when the user has an already-drafted review or reply and wants it posted: "post this review", "reply to this comment", "mark this thread resolved", "submit my review comments". Takes drafted content — from the built-in `code-review` skill's findings, from `courier/receive-feedback`'s response plan, or typed directly by the user — and posts it to GitHub via `gh pr review` or `gh pr comment`. Does not draft content itself; this skill is purely mechanical execution of something already written, gated by explicit user confirmation before any post fires.
- courier:pr: Trigger when the user asks to open a PR or write a PR description: "open a PR", "create a pull request", "write the PR description". Given a diff, a linked spec, and a linked requirement, produces a PR title and body a reviewer with zero context can act on, then opens the PR via `gh pr create` after user confirmation.
- courier:receive-feedback: Trigger when the user asks to process or triage incoming review feedback: "address the feedback", "respond to review comments", "what do these comments mean", "triage this review". Assembles a review package — diff summary, linked spec, test results, open questions — so the author has full context to respond without re-reading the whole thread. Does not categorize individual comments by priority; that's the caller's judgment call, made with `shared/references/delivery/github.md`'s vocabulary in hand. This is for feedback received on the user's own PR — critiquing someone else's PR is the built-in `code-review` skill's job, not this one.
- courier:release: Trigger when the user asks to cut a release or summarize what's in one: "cut a release", "what's in this release", "generate release notes". Aggregates changeset@2 entries since the last release into a release-artifact@2: filters consumer_impact: internal-only entries, computes the version as max(semver_impact) across the rest applied to the prior version, and carries each changeset's summary through unedited.
- muse:component: Trigger when the user asks to spec a UI component: "spec this component", "draft a component spec", "write a spec for this design", "audit this component spec", "is this component spec ready?", "gate this component spec". Given a requirement@1 or free-text design intent, produces a spec@1 covering props, variants, per-state observable behavior, and accessibility criteria as testable propositions. Every criterion is falsifiable from outside the implementation; error cases and invalid prop combinations carry is_error_case: true. No TBDs anywhere in the document — genuinely unknown items go in non_goals or the reasoning scratchpad instead. Gated by a binding exit gate before the spec proceeds to planning.
- navigator:plan: Trigger this skill when the user says "write a plan for X", "how do we implement this spec", "break this down into tasks", "what are the implementation steps", "create an implementation plan", or "plan this out". Also activate when a spec (spec@1) exists and the user is ready to move to implementation but hasn't broken it down yet. Produces a plan@1 artifact where every task includes exact file paths, a brief implementation approach, exact implementation code, the exact tests proving each criterion, a conventional commit message, and covers_criteria linking the task to specific acceptance criteria. spec_file_path and linked_requirement are propagated from the source spec. No TBDs. No "implement as appropriate." Every step is mechanically executable by a developer with zero domain context.
- ranger:audit: Find evidence-backed reachable defects in Rust, TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, or Go. Refute candidates, group defect families, and verify fixes against current code and the relevant execution boundary.
- scribe:architect: Trigger when `finding-report@2`, `implementation-review@2`, or `implementation-result@1` identifies a structural defect class. Produce the smallest `spec@1` that makes recurrence impossible or machine-detectable through a type, API, boundary, invariant, lint, test, or CI rule.
- scribe:audit-architecture: Trigger when a draft spec@1 needs checking against the workspace's whole-system architecture — not another spec, and not a single signature — before it reaches scribe/gate-spec: "check this spec against our architecture", "does this fit the system", "audit this against the arch model". Given a spec@1, checks it against the persisted arch-model@1 for boundary violations, competing abstractions, and invariant conflicts, building or refreshing the model first if it's absent or stale for the area the spec touches. Returns specific, rewritten fixes on fail, the same standard as scribe/audit-spec but at system scope instead of spec scope.
- scribe:audit-spec: Trigger when the user asks to review a spec's quality: "review this spec", "is this spec complete?", "audit this spec". Given a spec@1, adversarially reviews it for untestable criteria, ambiguous language, missing error cases, scope overlap with other specs, and incomplete sections. Returns a structured issue list with specific rewritten suggested fixes, not generic guidance. Named audit-spec rather than audit because the bare word audit is already ranger's plugin-level skill name (code/bug auditing) — a different domain entirely.
- scribe:correct-spec: Trigger when implementer reports that a spec criterion contradicts what the system actually does: a spec_contradiction status from smith. Given a spec_file_path, the criterion_id of the affected acceptance criterion, and a contradiction report (what the spec says vs. what the system actually does), revises the affected criterion — and any criteria that depend on it — and returns a corrected spec@1 with revision_note set. Use this when implementation reveals the spec itself is wrong, not merely hard to satisfy.
- scribe:draft-spec: Trigger when the user asks to write or draft a spec: "spec this out", "draft a spec", "write a spec for this requirement". Given a requirement@1 and optionally a research-report@1, produces a spec@1 draft with purpose, scope, non_goals, api_surface (if applicable), and acceptance criteria. Every criterion is a testable proposition; error cases carry is_error_case: true. No TBDs anywhere in the document — genuinely unknown items go in non_goals or the reasoning scratchpad instead.
- scribe:gate-spec: Trigger when a spec@1 needs a definitive pass/fail judgment before it enters planning: "gate this spec", "is this spec ready?", "check this spec before we plan it". Default disposition is fail — the spec must earn a pass. Passes only if every acceptance criterion is testable with no vague language, no TBDs remain, error cases are explicitly covered, and scope is narrow enough for one planning cycle. This gate checks the spec on its own terms — whole-system architectural fit is scribe/audit-architecture's job upstream, not re-litigated here. On fail, returns blockers specific enough for scribe/draft-spec to act on without further clarification.
- scribe:spec-drift: Trigger when the user asks whether implemented code still matches its spec, weeks or months after implementation: "check spec drift", "does the code still match this spec?", "has this spec drifted?". Given a spec@1 (via spec_file_path) and a workspace root, reads the spec from disk and the implementation from the workspace, and reports each criterion as covered (implemented and tested), uncovered (no matching implementation), or drifted (implementation exists but diverges from the criterion's contract). This is an on-demand diagnostic, not a blocking gate — scribe/gate-spec is the blocking gate.
- scribe:verify-spec: Trigger when the user asks whether a spec matches its source: "is this grounded?", "does this spec match the requirement?", "check this spec against the requirement". Given a draft spec@1 plus the originating requirement@1 and optional research-report@1, checks whether each acceptance criterion is grounded in the source artifacts. Classifies criteria as supported, unsupported, or overfitted. Collects evidence only — does not produce a pass/fail verdict. Use before implementation, not after — for post-implementation drift, use scribe/spec-drift instead.
- sentinel:gate: Trigger this skill when the user says "verify this", "check this spec", "check this plan", "check this requirement", "check this PR", "is this done?", "review this for completeness", "does this meet the criteria?", "gate this", or "quality check" — also before stage transitions: starting implementation from a spec, shipping from an implementation, opening a PR from a branch. Applies to any stage artifact: requirements, specs, plans, implementations, PRs. Do not activate for general Q&A, code explanation, or exploratory work with no artifact boundary being crossed. The gate either clears the artifact for the next stage or returns specific, actionable blockers to the producing agent.
- smith:implement: Activate for implementation, implementation tests, or behavior-preserving refactoring. Execute bounded batches with risk-based verification, defect-family review, and an independent scoped verdict. Do not activate for explanation-only requests.
- vanguard:research: Activate when the user says "I need to understand X before deciding", "is there a way to do Y", "what are the options for Z", "research this", "investigate this", "what does the codebase already do for X", "prior art on Y", or "what are the risks of approach Z" — also when the approach for a spec or plan is unclear, when checking what dependencies exist for a feature, or when any design question needs an evidence base before commitment. Investigates the question across internal sources (specs, docs, codebase patterns, manifests) and external sources as needed, then produces a research-report@1 that distinguishes confirmed findings from likely inferences from unverified assumptions, with a falsifiable recommendation and explicit confidence level so a spec writer (scribe) isn't surprised by implementation reality.
- weaver:audit-backlog: Trigger when the user asks about overall backlog health: "what's in the backlog", "audit the backlog", "what requirements are missing coverage". Cross-references all open requirement@1 objects against existing specs and implementation files. Returns per-requirement status (covered, partial, missing, duplicate) with evidence, plus a structured summary — per-status counts and an optional one-clause note, not a prose paragraph. Named audit-backlog rather than bare audit because that word is already ranger's plugin-level skill name (code/bug auditing) — a different domain entirely.
- weaver:capture-need: Trigger when the user describes a raw need in free text: "we need X", "the problem is Y", "users are asking for Z". Converts unstructured text into a structured requirement@1 draft — id, statement, stakeholder, why, done_when — without asking clarifying questions. Fields that cannot be inferred are omitted, not fabricated. out_of_scope is intentionally left empty for weaver/connect-requirement or a human to fill in.
- weaver:clarify-requirement: Trigger when a requirement@1 draft from weaver/capture-need has gaps to close before a spec can be written: "is this requirement complete?", "what's missing from this requirement". Given a requirement@1, evaluates gaps in priority order — testability of done_when, specificity of stakeholder, explicitness of out_of_scope — and either asks one focused question or returns the completed requirement with out_of_scope populated. One question per invocation, never a list.
- weaver:connect-requirement: Trigger when the user asks whether a specific requirement already exists or relates to other work: "is this already captured?", "does this overlap with an existing requirement?", "what does this relate to?". Given one requirement@1 (or a small named set), searches the workspace for related specs and implementation files, and checks for duplicate or overlapping requirements. Returns coverage status and duplicate_of references scoped to just the requirement(s) given — not a full backlog sweep.
- weaver:prioritize-backlog: Trigger when the user asks what to work on first from a set of requirements: "what should we prioritize", "rank the backlog", "what's most urgent". # oxc-react-docgen

10-100x faster drop-in replacement for react-docgen-typescript. OXC parses TypeScript/TSX; we extract React component props and emit RDT-compatible JSON. See `docs/STATUS.md` for current state and known gaps.

## Commands

```bash
cargo test -p oxc-react-docgen-core          # unit + snapshot tests
cargo clippy -p oxc-react-docgen-core -- -D warnings
cargo build --release                         # full build including CLI
```

Or use `/check` and `/snapshot` for the common workflows.

## Non-negotiables

1. No `unwrap()` outside `#[cfg(test)]` — use `?`
2. `FxHashMap` for internal maps; `BTreeMap` for JSON-output maps

# Pinned to callisto 0.8.0 in .github/workflows/release.yml.

# `match` is a package name ("<ecosystem>/<name>"), never a directory path.
# Root package.json is `oxc-react-docgen-workspace` so bare `oxc-react-docgen` stays unambiguous.

[changesets]
dir = ".changeset"

[cascade]
mode = "out-of-range"
bump-severity = "patch"
peer-escalation = true
preserve-npm-ranges = true

[[package]]
match = "cargo/oxc-react-docgen-core"
publish-to = ["crates-io"]
release-trigger = "changeset"

[[package]]
match = "cargo/oxc-react-docgen"
publish-to = ["crates-io"]
release-trigger = "changeset"

[[package]]
match = "npm/@oxc-react-docgen/cli"
publish-to = ["npm"]
release-trigger = "changeset"

# FFI shim: versioned with its npm wrapper, never published to crates.io.
[[package]]
match = "cargo/oxc-react-docgen-napi"
publish-to = []
release-trigger = "changeset"

[[package]]
match = "npm/@oxc-react-docgen/napi"
publish-to = ["npm"]
release-trigger = "changeset"

[[package]]
match = "npm/@oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin"
publish-to = ["npm"]
release-trigger = "changeset"

# The npm wrapper is meaningless without a matching binding build.
[[fixed-group]]
name = "napi-and-binding"
members = ["cargo/oxc-react-docgen-napi", "npm/@oxc-react-docgen/napi"]

# The npm wrapper redistributes this crate's binaries.
[[fixed-group]]
name = "cli-and-npm-wrapper"
members = ["cargo/oxc-react-docgen", "npm/@oxc-react-docgen/cli"]
=== release.yml ===
name: Release & Publish
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      release_source_sha:
        description: 'Merged Callisto release-PR commit to recover; leave empty for the triggering commit.'
        required: false
        type: string
permissions: {}
concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false
env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  RUST_VERSION: "1.98.1"
jobs:
  release-candidate:
    name: Identify a merged Callisto release PR
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    timeout-minutes: 10
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      is_release_pr: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.is_release_pr }}
      release_source_sha: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
    steps:
      - id: candidate
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA_INPUT: ${{ inputs.release_source_sha }}
          TRIGGERING_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          release_source_sha="${RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA_INPUT:-$TRIGGERING_SHA}"
          if [[ ! "$release_source_sha" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::release_source_sha must be exactly 40 lowercase hex characters"
            exit 1
          fi
          resolved_sha=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}" --jq '.sha')
          if [[ "$resolved_sha" != "$release_source_sha" ]]; then
            echo "::error::release_source_sha does not resolve to that exact commit"
            exit 1
          fi
          prs=$(gh api --paginate "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}/pulls" \
            --jq '[.[] | select(.merged_at != null and .base.ref == "main" and .head.repo.full_name == "'"${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"'" and (.head.ref == "callisto/version-packages" or (.head.ref | test("^callisto/version-packages--[0-9a-f]{40}$"))))] | length')
          verified=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}" --jq '.commit.verification.verified')
          if [[ "$prs" == 1 && "$verified" == true ]]; then
            {
              echo 'is_release_pr=true'
              echo "release_source_sha=$release_source_sha"
            } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo 'is_release_pr=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
  version-pr:
    name: Create or update the Callisto release PR
    needs: release-candidate
    if: >-
      needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release_pr != 'true' &&
      inputs.release_source_sha == ''
    timeout-minutes: 15
    concurrency:
      group: version-pr
      cancel-in-progress: false
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/setup-callisto@c5578e6a63754b54575b3ac7518cc1753e443393 # callisto@0.8.0
        with:
          version: callisto@0.8.0
          verification: require
      - name: Compose, version, and open the release PR
        uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-action@c5578e6a63754b54575b3ac7518cc1753e443393 # callisto@0.8.0
        with:
          setup_callisto: 'false'
          branch: main
          release_branch: callisto/version-packages
          version_command: 'callisto version --refresh-lockfiles'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
  plan:
    name: Derive release intent from the merged release commit
    needs: release-candidate
    if: needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release_pr == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 20
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/setup-callisto@c5578e6a63754b54575b3ac7518cc1753e443393 # callisto@0.8.0
        with:
          version: callisto@0.8.0
          verification: require
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          path: release-source
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Derive and hash intent
        env:
          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          handoff_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent"
          mkdir -p "$handoff_dir"
          callisto release plan --profile production \
            --source-root "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-source" \

    name: Execute approved release
      NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"
      # Needs callisto >= 0.9.0 (gitignored release-source files, platform-package publish).
      - uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/setup-callisto@c5578e6a63754b54575b3ac7518cc1753e443393 # callisto@0.8.0
          version: callisto@0.8.0
          path: release-source
      # Outside release-source: callisto rejects non-ignored untracked files there.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
      - name: Verify same-run handoff before credentials
        run: |
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/napi-artifacts
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/cli-artifacts
      - name: Install deps and place platform binaries
        run: |
          pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
          (cd packages/napi && pnpm napi artifacts --output-dir "${RUNNER_TEMP}/napi-artifacts")
            dest="packages/cli/npm/${platform}"
            mv "$dir"/* "$dest/"
          for dir in packages/napi/npm/* packages/cli/npm/*; do
      # npm and pnpm both read the user-level .npmrc.
      - name: Authenticate with the npm registry
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
        run: npm config set //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken "$NPM_TOKEN"
      - name: Execute verified release
        run: |
          receipt_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-release-receipt/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
          args=(
          callisto release execute "${args[@]}"
      - name: Summarize receipt
        run: |
          receipt="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-release-receipt/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}/release-receipt.json"
      - name: Upload receipt
          name: release-receipt
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/callisto-release-receipt/${{ github.run_id }}

1. **Remove `--profile production`** from both `callisto release plan` and `callisto release execute`. 0.9 deletes the flag (#133), so the job fails on argument parsing. You can do this today: in 0.8 `production` is already the default, so the flag does nothing.
2. **Bump the pins once 0.9.0 is tagged.** There are four refs: three `setup-callisto`, one `callisto-action`. Also update `version: callisto@0.9.0` and the "Pinned to callisto 0.8.0" header line in `callisto.toml`. The stack is still open and release PR #113 hasn't merged, so there's no tag to pin yet.

**Already correct in #9**
- `--state` and `--recovery` are already gone; 0.9 removes both. Recovery is now just re-running the workflow with `release_source_sha`, and callisto's own workflow does the same.
- Platform packages under `npm/<platform>`, outside the pnpm workspace globs and attached through `optionalDependencies`: 0.9 supports this layout directly. Its test fixture is literally commented "oxc-react-docgen's shape", and it publishes those packages before their owner.
- Binaries are placed in `release-source`, and `*.node` plus the CLI binaries are gitignored. That matches 0.9's rule that the release checkout contain no untracked files that aren't ignored.
- `callisto.toml` needs no key changes. Scoped npm packages default to `public`, and #9 sets `publishConfig.access` anyway.
- Without a `[release]` section, 0.9 plans no artifact uploads and ignores `--orchestration-revision`, so #9's "reject unexpected artifact slots" check is still right.
- Nothing calls a removed command: `validate`, `publish`, `plan-publish`, `tag` or `filter-plan`.

**Don't adopt**
- **The workflow `callisto init` generates.** `init` refuses to run when `callisto.toml` already exists. Its build matrix covers the napi package (#144 now finds `crates/binding` correctly) but not the CLI platform packages, so #9's hand-written build job is still needed.
- **Renaming to `callisto-release.yml`.** 0.9 ties build-attestation checks to that filename, but only for binaries declared in `[release]`. We don't declare any.
- **Pinning callisto in `.prototools` (#142).** The proto plugin doesn't verify checksums yet. `setup-callisto` with `verification: require` is the stronger guarantee, so keep it.

**Your call:** #9 removes the `environment: release` reviewer gate. With that gone, merging a version PR publishes to crates.io and npm with no approval step, while `NPM_TOKEN` and `id-token: write` sit in that job. Callisto's docs recommend keeping the gate.

Minor: GitHub release notes will now come from each `CHANGELOG.md` section instead of being auto-generated (#126). No change needed.

Want me to push the `--profile` removal to #9 now and bump the pins when 0.9.0 is tagged?

# callisto-cli

## 0.10.0

- Output that explains why a package is released reports `release-trigger`, fixed groups, linked groups, the tag template and pre-major inference as configured when you set them, instead of "(default)".
- `snapshot` works for PyPI packages: their snapshot version and dependents' specs use PEP 440.
- Git errors that came from parsing git's own output now have specific codes and help text, instead of one generic git error code.
- release, release plan, release execute, release artifact-manifest, and release-pr's JSON output now carry schemaVersion, command, and dryRun fields like every other command's JSON output.
- `callisto release-pr verify` accepts `callisto release-pr decide --format json` output as-is again, so the release action can open and update the release PR. 0.9.0 failed with E281.
- Adding a package with the same name in another ecosystem needs no configuration: the existing package keeps its release history, tags and changelog, and new tags use the qualified name (`cargo/foo@1.1.0`). A pre-release cycle started before the new package keeps working. A changeset that names a now-ambiguous `foo` fails with E103 and shows the qualified form to write.
- init now names the exact file it failed to write when a write fails, instead of a pathless error.
- In pre-release mode, packages with the same name in two ecosystems (`cargo/foo`, `npm/foo`) keep separate starting versions in `pre.json` instead of sharing one.
- `callisto release` no longer fails with E167 when GitHub is slow to show a release or asset it just created, uploaded or published; it waits up to a minute.

## 0.9.0

- callisto release --dry-run and callisto release plan now include a diagnostics array in their JSON output when an artifact owner package is selected without its product package, instead of only printing a stderr warning.
- callisto version now refreshes npm, pnpm, yarn, bun and pdm lockfiles by default (in addition to Cargo, uv and poetry), opt out with --no-refresh-lockfiles; a failed refresh now stops the command with a coded error naming the lockfile and command
- A dependent released in the same run has its spec on a bumped internal dependency raised to the new version, even when the old spec still covers it.
- Generated release workflows pass the detected default branch to the release-PR action, and `init` now resolves it from a live remote query or the checked-out branch when `origin/HEAD` isn't set locally, instead of silently defaulting to `main`.
- **Git runs through the system `git` binary only**
  
  The in-process gitoxide backend is gone; every Git read and write already had to work through the `git` binary the CLI requires. Commit inference keeps a commit that touched a package even when a later merge discarded its change (`git log --full-history`), matching the removed backend. An annotated release tag made with no Git identity configured takes the target commit's committer as its tagger.
  
  Breaking:
  - `callisto_model::vcs` (was `callisto-vcs`): removed `GitRepository`, `ShellGit`, the `GitDataSource` trait and the revwalk visit counter. `GitAccess::discover(root, runner)` is now `GitAccess::new(root, runner)` with inherent methods.
  - `callisto_model::vcs`: `commits_since` with an unresolvable `since` ref returns `VcsError::RefNotFound` (was `VcsError::Git` from the shell path).
- Shell completions no longer offer hidden plumbing subcommands, at any nesting depth
- snapshot rewrites every dependency spec the snapshot version falls outside of, so cargo metadata resolves after a snapshot
- Loading a workspace now fails with a clear error naming both directories when two of them declare the same ecosystem and name, instead of silently routing dependency edges to the wrong package.
- Fixed groups compute their shared version from the highest member version when no member is tagged, support PEP 440 versions, and follow pre-release mode. Before, an untagged group could be bumped down to 0.x.
- `callisto init` can generate `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml` (the workflow path release artifact attestations are bound to) for a workspace with no napi/maturin platform packages and no shipped release artifacts: interactive question or `--workflow`/`--no-workflow` (mutually exclusive), refuses to overwrite an existing file (checked before the preview, including under `--dry-run`). After writing the file, init prints that a merge to the default branch publishes, so that branch should require pull requests and reviews. JSON output carries the same text as a `workflow-merge-publishes` diagnostic with the new `info` severity. The generated file is two jobs (`version-pr`, `release`) under 40 lines, triggered on push to the detected default branch, with per-job permissions and secrets wired per detected ecosystem (`CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, `PYPI_TOKEN`; npm workspaces also set `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE` so publishes carry provenance), pinned to `orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-action@<commit>` -- resolved from the `callisto@<version>` release tag, since a GitHub Actions `uses:` ref is split at the *last* `@` in the string, so the tag can't be written into `uses:` directly.
  
  `callisto-action` gains a `mode: version-pr | release` input (default `version-pr`, unchanged behavior); `mode: release` installs Callisto and runs `callisto release`, filling `published`/`publishedPackages` from its receipt. An invalid mode fails naming the accepted values. Its environment-setup step no longer references sibling action `setup-callisto` through `uses:` (`$/` and an external `owner/repo/path@ref` both resolve against whichever ref invoked the *top-level* workflow, not necessarily this action's own) -- it now calls `setup-callisto`'s install script directly by `github.action_path`, so it always uses its own checked-out ref, including when invoked from another repository's workflow.
- Workspace discovery no longer silently drops or misattaches packages: a manifest that fails to parse now fails with a clear error naming the path when it's a real workspace member, and warns otherwise; root detection asks git itself instead of hand-walking for .git, so GIT_DIR and worktrees are respected, and it reads [workspace]/[package] as real TOML tables instead of matching the text (a commented-out mention no longer counts); a platform package sitting beside its own Cargo.toml or pyproject.toml is never misattached to an unrelated owner; and a [[package]] rule that matches no packages gets a warning, matching the existing [[package-set]] one.
- Every add/version/schema/pre/release-pr error now carries its own code and help text instead of a generic message; release-pr decide/verify report the exact invalid-branch or duplicate-pull-request code instead of a plain string when reading a snapshot or decision from a file, inline JSON, or stdin.
- callisto init and callisto release --dry-run in a repository without an origin remote no longer print a stray git error about the missing remote.
- **`callisto init` asks for intent and previews the first release**
  
  `init` prints what it detected (ecosystems, packages, `origin`, last tags, binaries), then asks only for versioning mode and, when a package builds a binary, whether to ship binaries (product package, GitHub repository, target triples). It shows the resulting `callisto.toml` and the first release plan from the same derivation as `release --dry-run`, then writes after confirmation. Non-default tag conventions (`{name}-v{version}`, `{name}-{version}`, `v{version}`) are detected and kept. Non-interactive: `--yes --versioning <fixed|independent>`, plus `--artifact-target`, `--forge-repository`, `--product-package` to ship binaries. In a repository with no commit yet, `init` writes the config and skips the preview.

- name: Compose, version, and open the release PR
        uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-action@c5578e6a63754b54575b3ac7518cc1753e443393 # callisto@0.8.0
        with:
          setup_callisto: 'false'
          branch: main
          release_branch: callisto/version-packages
          # Core bumps otherwise leave path-dependents stale in Cargo.lock.
          version_command: 'callisto version --refresh-lockfiles'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          handoff_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent"
          mkdir -p "$handoff_dir"
          callisto release plan --profile production \
            --source-root "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-source" \
            --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA" \
            --from-release-commit "$RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA" \
            --decision "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-source/.callisto/release-decision.json" \
            --out "$handoff_dir/release-intent.json"
          shasum -a 256 "$handoff_dir/release-intent.json" > "$handoff_dir/release-intent.json.sha256"
      # No `[release]` section here, so callisto-managed artifact slots are unexpected.
          args=(
            --source-root "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-source"
            --intent "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent/release-intent.json"
            --receipt "$receipt_dir/release-receipt.json"
            --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA"
            --profile production
          )
          callisto release execute "${args[@]}"
      - name: Summarize receipt
